To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the choice of IP strategies is influenced by the innovating firms’ age and R&D intensity and that the choice of formal and informal IP strategies are complementary, especially for firms that introduce more radical innovations.

(1) Young highly innovative firms are more likely to choose a combination of formal and informal strategies to appropriate their innovations than firms that are not highly innovative; (2) They are particularly more prone to choose secrecy as a strategy to appropriate returns from their innovations; (3) This is particularly the case for young highly innovative firms when they introduce radical innovations new to markets; (4) The results hold when we control for firm and industry characteristics.
young highly innovative companies tend to combine formal and non formal mechanisms to appropriate the returns of their innovations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the appropriability strategies of young highly-innovative companies.
a particular type of young firms that are both young and highly R&D intensive.
the question of which IP strategies young highly innovative firms choose and how these strategies relate to their innovative performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
young firms that introduce highly innovative products to the market tend to rely on secrecy and patents.
firms that are young and highly R&D intensive are more likely to use secrecy as an IP strategy, especially when their innovations are new to the market.
the more innovative a firm is, the more likely it will be to use a variety of formal and informal IP protection strategies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
young highly innovative companies combine different strategies to appropriate the returns of their innovations.
the young highly innovative firms are likely to choose a combination of strategies.
the choice of IP strategy is a function of a firm’s innovative profile, the nature of the innovation and the firm’s market position.
The main takeaway from our work is that
firms with a high innovation profile and a young age are more likely to use secrecy as a strategy to appropriate the value of their innovation.
the choice of IP strategies is not only driven by the characteristics of the technology, but also by the characteristics of firms.
young highly innovative firms are likely to use multiple IP strategies to appropriate the returns to their innovations.
